subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept sha256+size SQLite provenance as the permanent trust mechanism for generated HTML that is staged into media/outbound and later reloaded with host-read enabled?
rationale: The implementation appears fail-closed and content-bound, but it deliberately extends a local HTML host-read trust boundary beyond the temp root, which automation should not approve on behalf of maintainers.

options.title: Accept provenance-gated trust
options.body: Treat the SQLite provenance row plus same-buffer sha256/size verification as sufficient to carry generated-HTML trust through outbound staging, then merge after normal exact-head gates.

options.title: Tighten lifecycle first
options.body: Require additional lifecycle constraints such as TTL-based row pruning or chunked stale-row deletion before accepting the new stored trust surface.

options.title: Reject staged HTML trust
options.body: Keep outbound-staged HTML blocked and rely on PDF or another non-HTML workaround until a different security design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept provenance-gated trust
recommendation.body: Treat the SQLite provenance row plus same-buffer sha256/size verification as sufficient to carry generated-HTML trust through outbound staging, then merge after normal exact-head gates.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam and have the clearest history signal for accepting or redirecting this boundary.
